Concluding at 272/10 (114.4 ov), Pakistan posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Pakistan posted 272/10 (114.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, South Africa countered with 201/10 (65.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 7-Wicket Spell: Hasan Ali (7/48), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Hasan Ali delivered a masterclass for Pakistan (13 Runs & 12 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Pakistan 53%) and allowing Pakistan to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, South Africa faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Pakistan's bowling unit, bolstered by Faheem Ashraf (107 Runs & 1 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Pakistan won by 95 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Pakistan's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While South Africa produced fighting phases, Pakistan won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
